claim_ceiling: Machine visual description of the official f57v and opposite-side f57r canvases only; no label ownership, word, role value, language, cipher, plaintext, meaning, or translation is established.

observations.observation: A large circular diagram occupies the upper portion of the folio, while the lower portion is mostly blank.
Four annular writing bands surround a central circular compartment.
Four human figures are arranged radially around a six-lobed central rosette; their heads are oriented inward toward the rosette while their torsos and arms extend outward or sideways.
Four short figure-near inscriptions occupy the same central compartment, and four further inscriptions run radially outward in the gaps between consecutive figures.
No drawn leader line, bracket, or separate enclosure visibly assigns any figure-near inscription to one specific figure.
The radial inscriptions lie between figures rather than pointing to figure centers; they are text baselines, not graphic connector lines.
An isolated label lies just outside the upper-left part of the outer circle near aligned start marks crossing the annular bands.
A pale blue-green wash is visible beneath and below the diagram, and a separate dark mark appears near the lower-right page margin.
The opposite side of the same leaf, f57r, carries a large plant with extensive green-painted leaf masses whose mirrored positions correspond to the diffuse pale green forms visible on f57v.
The f57v green wash is reverse-side show-through or pigment penetration from f57r rather than a separate wash applied as part of the f57v circular diagram.
The ordinary-light scans alone do not distinguish optical translucency through the parchment from physical migration of green pigment through it.
